title: What Is a Kegel and Where Is the Pelvic Muscle?
summary: The pelvic floor is a layer of muscle stretched like a hammock across the base of the pelvis. A Kegel works this muscle by squeezing and relaxing it.
shortSummary: The pelvic floor muscle and how to train it

sections.title: Where is the pelvic floor?
sections.text: The pelvic floor muscles are a layer of muscle running from the pubic bone at the front to the tailbone at the back, and between the two sitting bones at the sides. Like a hammock, they carry the bladder and bowel from below; the urethra and anus pass through these muscles.

sections.title: What does it do?
sections.text: These muscles let you hold in urine and wind, and empty the last drops left in the urethra after urinating. During an erection, the muscles near the base of the penis make it harder for blood to flow back out, helping keep the erection; ejaculation also happens through rhythmic contractions of these muscles.

sections.title: How do you find the muscle?
sections.text: Imagine squeezing your anus to hold in wind, or trying to hold in urine. When you squeeze the right muscle, your anus draws in and up, the base of your penis lifts slightly and your testicles rise a little. You can check in front of a mirror or while sitting.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.text: Tensing the belly, glutes or legs; holding your breath; forgetting to let the muscle go. Also, don't stop your urine flow midstream as an exercise; it can stop the bladder from emptying fully. This can be tried at most once, only to get to know the muscle.

sections.title: Where does the Kegel come from?
sections.text: The exercise is named after Arnold Kegel, the American gynaecologist who described and popularised these exercises in the 1940s. Today pelvic floor exercises are also being studied in men for urine dribbling, erection problems and premature ejaculation.

sections.title: When does it show results?
sections.text: With regular training, it usually takes 3–6 months to see a clear difference. As with any muscle, consistency matters more than intensity.

sections.title: In the app
sections.text: Today's workout shows you when to squeeze and when to relax on the screen and through vibration. You can refresh the correct technique with Profile > Replay the lesson.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: NHS, pelvic floor exercises for men information leaflets. Dorey et al., BJU International (2005).

title: Why does premature ejaculation happen?
summary: Ejaculating much earlier than wanted and being unable to control it. It's common and can often be improved.
shortSummary: Common, and can often be improved

sections.title: When is it called premature ejaculation?
sections.text: Experts look at three criteria: ejaculation happening very quickly almost every time, being unable to delay it, and it causing distress. In the lifelong type, ejaculation usually happens within 1 minute of penetration; in the acquired type, the time drops markedly, mostly below 3 minutes.

sections.title: How common is it?
sections.text: Up to 20–30% of men describe themselves as ejaculating too early. Far fewer meet all the diagnostic criteria: about 2–3% for the lifelong type and about 4% for the acquired type.

sections.title: Why does it happen?
sections.text: In the lifelong type, a biological tendency related to the brain's serotonin system and to genetics stands out. In the acquired type, common causes are erection problems (rushing out of fear of losing the erection), prostate inflammation, excess thyroid hormone, performance anxiety, stress and relationship problems.

sections.title: A vicious circle
sections.text: Ejaculating early once creates anxiety, and anxiety makes ejaculation even quicker the next time. Noticing this circle is the first step to breaking it.

sections.title: What does it do?
sections.text: The pelvic floor muscle plays a direct role in the ejaculation reflex. In a study of 40 men with lifelong premature ejaculation, after 12 weeks of pelvic floor exercises 33 of them (82%) gained control over ejaculation, and the average time rose from under 1 minute to about 2.5 minutes. The stop-start technique, reducing anxiety and talking openly with your partner also help. If the problem continues, there are also effective treatments a urologist can suggest.

sections.title: In the app
sections.text: In Kegel training, the Quick Squeeze teaches you to know the muscle, and the Relax and Breathe part teaches you to let it go consciously. Ejaculation control relies on both together.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: Serefoglu et al., ISSM definition of premature ejaculation, Sexual Medicine (2014). Pastore et al., Therapeutic Advances in Urology (2014).

title: Why do erection problems happen?
summary: Not being able to get or keep an erection firm enough for sex. It's common and often linked to blood vessel health.
shortSummary: Common; often linked to blood vessel health

sections.title: When is it considered a problem?
sections.text: Occasionally not getting an erection can happen to anyone because of tiredness, alcohol or stress. When the problem becomes regular and starts to affect sex, it's called erectile dysfunction.

sections.title: How does it happen?
sections.text: An erection is a chain: a nerve signal from the brain widens the blood vessels in the penis, blood fills them and the pelvic floor muscles make it harder for that blood to flow back out. A problem at any link in the chain makes an erection harder.

sections.title: Common causes
sections.text: Physical causes: hardened arteries, diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, excess weight, smoking, alcohol and some medicines. Psychological causes: performance anxiety, stress, depression and relationship problems. Psychological causes are more common in younger men, and vascular causes in older men.

sections.title: An early warning from the heart
sections.text: The blood vessels of the penis are narrower than those of the heart, so blood vessel problems can show up first in erections. In men followed for more than 11 years on average, those with erection problems had a higher risk of cardiovascular disease. A lasting erection problem is a good reason to have your heart health checked too.

sections.title: What does it do?
sections.text: In a randomised study of 55 men with erection problems, after 6 months of pelvic floor exercises and lifestyle changes, 40% of the men regained normal erections and about a third improved. Regular movement, weight control, quitting smoking and drinking less support blood vessel health. When these aren't enough, there are also effective medicines.

sections.title: In the app
sections.text: The Long Squeeze and Endurance exercises work the muscles that help keep an erection. If you smoke, the Smoke-Free Camp can also support you on this path.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: Dorey et al., BJU International (2005). Massachusetts Male Aging Study, Journal of the American College of Cardiology (2010).

title: Is there such a thing as masturbation addiction?
summary: Masturbation is a normal and common behaviour. The problem is less about frequency and more about losing control and life being affected negatively.
shortSummary: The problem isn't frequency, it's loss of control

sections.title: Is masturbation harmful?
sections.text: No. Masturbation is a common and healthy sexual behaviour at every age; there's no scientific evidence that it causes infertility, vision problems or loss of strength. In a study of more than 3,400 men aged 18–35, no link was found between how often they masturbated and erection problems.

sections.title: Is it an official diagnosis?
sections.text: There's no official diagnosis called masturbation addiction. The World Health Organization's classification (ICD-11) instead includes compulsive sexual behaviour disorder, which is defined not as an addiction but as an impulse control problem.

sections.title: When does it become a problem?
sections.text: Frequency isn't what matters. It can be a problem if someone can't control it despite wanting to stop for months, if the behaviour comes before work, sleep, relationships and responsibilities, and if it continues even though it's no longer enjoyable. In a study of more than 2,300 adults in the US, about 10% of men reported having difficulty controlling their sexual urges and feeling marked distress about it.

sections.title: Feelings of guilt
sections.text: Some people feel addicted because the behaviour conflicts with their moral or religious values. According to experts, distress arising only from this conflict isn't enough for a diagnosis; but the distress is real and worth thinking about.

sections.title: What can be done?
sections.text: Notice the situations that trigger the behaviour: loneliness, stress, boredom or the phone late at night. Small changes help, such as charging the phone outside the bedroom, moving during the day and doing a few minutes of breathing when an urge comes. If the loss of control continues, the most researched approach for this is cognitive behavioural therapy.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: WHO ICD-11, Compulsive sexual behaviour disorder (6C72). Dickenson et al., JAMA Network Open (2018). JMIR Public Health and Surveillance (2021), study of 3,419 men.

title: Not lasting long in bed
summary: Often the problem isn't the time but the expectation. Knowing the real averages and improving control helps.
shortSummary: Often the problem isn't the time, it's the expectation

sections.title: What is the real average?
sections.text: In a study across five countries, including Türkiye, in which 500 couples timed sex with a stopwatch, the median time from penetration to ejaculation was 5.4 minutes. Times varied a lot from person to person and got shorter with age.

sections.title: How long is enough?
sections.text: In a survey of sex therapists, 3–7 minutes of intercourse was rated as adequate and 7–13 minutes as desirable. Very long times weren't rated as better.

sections.title: Where do the expectations come from?
sections.text: Films and adult content show staged, edited scenes. These images can create a false yardstick for how long real sex lasts and increase performance anxiety.

sections.title: Things that shorten the time
sections.text: Anxiety, not having had sex for a long time, very intense arousal, rushing out of fear of losing the erection, and weak or constantly tense pelvic floor muscles can shorten the time.

sections.title: What does it do?
sections.text: Pelvic floor exercises can increase control over the ejaculation reflex. Stopping when ejaculation approaches and waiting for the urge to fade (stop-start), breathing slowly and deeply, changing rhythm or position and spending more time on foreplay also help.

sections.title: In the app
sections.text: The Quick Squeeze teaches you to know the muscle, and the Relax and Breathe part teaches you to let it go consciously. Control depends as much on being able to relax the muscle whenever you want as on squeezing it hard.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: Waldinger et al., Journal of Sexual Medicine (2005). Corty and Guardiani, Journal of Sexual Medicine (2008). Pastore et al., Therapeutic Advances in Urology (2014).

title: Thinking you can't satisfy your partner
summary: It's a common worry and often doesn't reflect reality. Communication and closeness shape satisfaction more than time or size.

sections.title: Why is this worry so common?
sections.text: Many men see their partner's satisfaction as a grade for their own performance. This pressure can lead to performance anxiety, and anxiety to erection and ejaculation problems. Research shows that performance anxiety is an important cause of erection problems, especially in young men.

sections.title: Facts about orgasm
sections.text: Only about 18% of women report being able to orgasm from penetration alone; for most, clitoral stimulation is needed or makes orgasm easier. If your partner doesn't orgasm from penetration alone, it's not your failure; it's very common.

sections.title: The orgasm gap
sections.text: In a study of more than 52,000 adults in the US, 95% of heterosexual men and 65% of women said they usually or always orgasm during sex. Women who orgasmed more often more frequently reported longer foreplay, oral sex, loving words and being able to say what they wanted.

sections.title: Size worries
sections.text: An analysis combining measurements from more than 15,000 men found the average erect penis length to be about 13 cm. Most men who feel small are actually within the average range.

sections.title: What does it do?
sections.text: Asking your partner what they like and sharing your own wishes is the most effective but least used approach. Making time for foreplay, not focusing only on penetration and aiming to enjoy it together rather than to perform reduce anxiety.

sections.title: In the app
sections.text: Pelvic floor training can support erections and ejaculation control. The breathing tools can also help you reduce tension before sex.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: Herbenick et al., Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy (2018). Frederick et al., Archives of Sexual Behavior (2018). Veale et al., BJU International (2015).

title: Why do morning erections happen?
summary: They're erections that happen by themselves during sleep. They're a natural sign of a healthy blood vessel and nerve system.
shortSummary: A natural sign of healthy blood vessels and nerves

sections.title: Why does it happen?
sections.text: In the dreaming REM stage of sleep, the brain reduces the signals that hold back erections and blood flow to the penis increases. That's why healthy men usually have 3–5 erections a night, each lasting about 25–35 minutes. You notice it in the morning because you wake up during the last REM period.

sections.title: What do they show?
sections.text: These erections aren't related to sexual thoughts; they show that the blood vessels, nerves and hormones are working properly. Experts see continued morning and night-time erections in a man with erection problems as a clue that the problem may be more psychological, such as anxiety or stress.

sections.title: What if they don't happen at all?
sections.text: Missing them for a morning or two doesn't matter; late nights, alcohol and tiredness often affect them. If you've had no morning erections at all for weeks, it may be a sign of a blood vessel, hormone or sleep problem and is worth having checked.

sections.title: What affects them?
sections.text: Problems that disrupt sleep such as sleep apnoea, not enough sleep, alcohol, some medicines, older age and low testosterone can reduce morning erections.

sections.title: In the app
sections.text: Regular Kegel training works the muscles that help keep an erection. Enough regular sleep matters at least as much as training.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: Clinical reviews on penile tumescence during sleep (Journal of Family Practice, 1994; Andrologia, 2005).

title: Why does low sexual desire happen?
summary: Desire drops from time to time for everyone. If it lasts a long time, it's usually related to stress, sleep, mood, the relationship or hormones.
shortSummary: Stress, sleep and the relationship can affect desire

sections.title: When is it considered a problem?
sections.text: Desire changes from period to period; a busy job, tiredness or an anxious time naturally affect it. It's considered a problem when sexual thoughts and desire drop markedly for months and this bothers you or your relationship. In a study of more than 12,000 middle-aged men, this rate was about 5%.

sections.title: Common causes
sections.text: Stress and a heavy workload, depression and anxiety, relationship problems and poor communication, avoiding sex after having erection or ejaculation problems, too much alcohol, some medicines (for example some antidepressants and blood pressure medicines) and low testosterone.

sections.title: Sleep and testosterone
sections.text: In a study of healthy young men, sleeping just 5 hours a night for a single week lowered daytime testosterone levels by 10–15%, and participants felt less energetic. Regular, sufficient sleep is an important foundation for desire.

sections.title: Testosterone isn't everything
sections.text: Low testosterone can reduce desire; however, according to experts, especially at older ages there's no one-to-one link between desire and blood testosterone levels. Desire is shaped by body, mind and relationship together.

sections.title: What does it do?
sections.text: Sorting out your sleep, moving, drinking less and managing stress are the first steps. Talking with your partner without pressure and not limiting closeness to sex alone also help desire come back. Long-lasting low desire needs its cause looked into.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: European Association of Urology (EAU), Sexual and reproductive health guidelines: Low sexual desire. Leproult and Van Cauter, JAMA (2011).

title: Why do urine dribbling and leaking happen?
summary: The last drops after urinating and sudden urges are very common. The pelvic floor muscles play a direct role here.
shortSummary: Last drops are common; the pelvic floor helps

sections.title: Dribbling after urinating
sections.text: A few drops of urine coming out after you've urinated and zipped up can happen to men of any age. Normally, a muscle at the base of the penis reflexively squeezes out the urine left in the urethra after you finish; when this muscle weakens, a little urine stays in the urethra and dribbles out later.

sections.title: Types of leaking
sections.text: Leaking when coughing, sneezing or lifting something heavy is called stress incontinence. A sudden urge that makes it hard to reach the toilet in time is called urge incontinence. In men, leaking is often linked to an enlarged prostate or prostate surgery.

sections.title: What does it do?
sections.text: In a study of men with erection problems and urine dribbling, after 6 months of pelvic floor exercises the dribbling complaint disappeared completely in 75% of participants. Part of the exercise in the study was squeezing the muscle hard right after finishing urinating to empty the urethra.

sections.title: A tip that works straight away
sections.text: After you finish urinating, squeeze your pelvic floor muscle hard a few times. If you like, you can also gently press with your fingers from behind the testicles towards the penis to empty the urine left in the urethra.

sections.title: When does it matter?
sections.text: Blood in the urine, pain or burning, going to the toilet very often, a markedly weaker flow or feeling as if you can't empty your bladder are symptoms that need checking.

sections.title: In the app
sections.text: The Long Squeeze and Endurance exercises strengthen these muscles. The Quick Squeeze teaches you to switch the muscle on fast when you cough or sneeze.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: Dorey et al., Urologic Nursing (2004). Dorey, Physiotherapy (2002), review of post-micturition dribble.

title: A tense pelvic floor and pelvic pain
summary: The pelvic floor muscle can be not only weak but constantly tense. This can lead to pain and to urinary and sexual problems.
shortSummary: The muscle may not be weak but constantly tense

sections.title: What does a tense muscle mean?
sections.text: In some men the pelvic floor muscle stays slightly contracted all the time because of stress, sitting for long periods or habit. A muscle that can't relax can't do its job well, just like a weak one.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.text: Ongoing pain or pressure in the groin, perineum (between the testicles and anus), penis or testicles, or lower abdomen; straining or burning when urinating; pain during or after ejaculation. This picture is often called chronic prostatitis or chronic pelvic pain syndrome, and in most cases there's no infection.

sections.title: How common is it?
sections.text: In a large study in the US, about 2% of men had symptoms of this syndrome; in different studies the lifetime rate ranges from 2% to 10%.

sections.title: What does it do?
sections.text: Physical therapy focused on relaxing the muscle is one of the most researched approaches. In a pilot study of women and men, 57% of those who received pelvic-specific physical therapy reported marked improvement, compared with 21% in the general massage group. Slow, deep breathing, warm showers, breaks from long sitting and reducing stress also help.

sections.title: Caution
sections.text: If you have pelvic pain, don't load up only on squeezing exercises; it's important to learn to let the muscle go completely first. If the pain continues or gets worse, it needs checking.

sections.title: In the app
sections.text: The Relax and Breathe part at the end of every workout teaches you to let the muscle go consciously. A Kegel isn't just squeezing; it's being able to squeeze and then relax completely.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: FitzGerald et al., Journal of Urology (2009). RAND RICE study, prevalence of chronic prostatitis and chronic pelvic pain syndrome.

title: The pelvic floor after prostate surgery
summary: Urine leakage is common after prostate surgery and often decreases over months. Pelvic floor exercises are widely recommended during this time.
shortSummary: Leaking is common and often decreases

sections.title: Why does leaking happen?
sections.text: The prostate is one of the structures that surround the urethra and help hold in urine. After surgery to remove the prostate, the job of holding in urine falls largely to the muscle surrounding the urethra and to the pelvic floor muscles.

sections.title: What to expect?
sections.text: In the first weeks after surgery, leaking is common, especially when coughing, standing up or lifting something heavy. In most men, control improves gradually and by itself within the first year.

sections.title: How effective is exercise?
sections.text: Reviews that combine research show that pelvic floor exercises may support recovery; however, according to a Cochrane review, how much extra benefit exercise alone provides isn't yet clear. Still, it's a safe, cheap and widely recommended method.

sections.title: When do you start?
sections.text: It's usually recommended to start pelvic floor exercises before surgery and continue after the catheter is removed. Don't exercise while a catheter is in place; decide when to start based on the advice of your surgical team.

sections.title: Erections
sections.text: Erection problems are also common after surgery, and recovery can take months, sometimes a year or two. The pelvic floor muscle also helps keep an erection.

sections.title: In the app
sections.text: Workouts start at Level 1 with short, light sessions. If it's too hard, your feedback lowers the level automatically, so you can progress at your own pace.

sections.title: Sources
sections.text: Anderson et al., Cochrane (2015), Conservative management for urinary incontinence after prostatectomy. Umbrella review of pelvic floor muscle training (2022).

title: What does level mean?
summary: How hard your workout is. It goes from 1 to 30.
shortSummary: How hard your workout is: from 1 to 30

sections.title: In short
sections.text: Your level decides how long and how hard your daily workout is. Level 1 takes about 4 minutes, Level 30 about 8 minutes.

sections.title: How does it change?
sections.text: It adjusts automatically from the feedback you give after each workout: say Too easy and it goes up a level; say Just right 3 times in a row and it goes up a level; say Hard and it goes down a level.

sections.title: I couldn't finish
sections.text: If you say I couldn't finish, your level goes down by one and you repeat the same plan day tomorrow.

sections.title: Changing it yourself
sections.text: You can also change your level yourself in Profile > Training. The higher the level, the longer the session.

title: What is the 30-day plan?
summary: A plan of one workout a day that tracks your progress.
shortSummary: A plan of one workout a day

sections.title: In short
sections.text: The plan has 30 days. Each day gets a workout prepared for that day's level, and the days you complete are ticked off.

sections.title: How is a workout built?
sections.text: Every workout starts with a light warm-up, continues with the main part and ends with relaxation and breathing. From Level 5, an endurance part is added too.

sections.title: When the plan ends
sections.text: When the 30 days are complete, a new plan starts automatically and your level carries on from where it was.

title: What do the exercise types mean?
summary: The six different exercises you meet in the workouts.
shortSummary: The six different exercises in the workouts

sections.title: Long Squeeze
sections.text: You squeeze the muscle, hold it for a few seconds, then relax completely.

sections.title: Quick Squeeze
sections.text: You squeeze for 1 second and relax for 1 second. It should be fast and controlled.

sections.title: Elevator
sections.text: You squeeze harder and harder in three stages, hold at the top, then release stage by stage.

sections.title: Rhythm
sections.text: Blocks of short, rhythmic squeeze pulses; you rest between blocks.

sections.title: Endurance
sections.text: A single long squeeze followed by a long rest.

sections.title: Relax and Breathe
sections.text: At the end of the workout, you consciously release the muscles with deep breathing.

title: What is the vibration language?
summary: Vibration signals that let you train without looking at the screen.
shortSummary: Signals that let you train without looking at the screen

sections.title: SQUEEZE
sections.text: A single strong vibration tells you it's time to squeeze. While squeezing, you feel a light tick every second.

sections.title: RELAX
sections.text: A light double vibration means it's time to relax.

sections.title: Done
sections.text: A triple vibration shows the exercise is over.

sections.title: Strength setting
sections.text: You can set the vibration strength to Off, Light, Normal or Strong in Profile > Training.

title: What is a streak?
summary: How many days in a row you've completed your daily workout.
shortSummary: How many days in a row you've trained

sections.title: In short
sections.text: Every day you complete the day's main workout, your streak goes up by one.

sections.title: When does it reset?
sections.text: If you haven't trained yet today but did yesterday, your streak continues. If you miss a whole day, the streak resets.

sections.title: How many sessions a day?
sections.text: 1 session a day is enough for your streak. You can raise your daily goal to up to 3 sessions in Profile > Training.

title: What is the strength test?
summary: A short weekly measurement so you can see your progress.

sections.title: Test A · Hold time
sections.text: You keep the button pressed while squeezing the muscle and let go as soon as you relax. You do a few attempts and the best one is saved.

sections.title: Test B · Quick contractions
sections.text: It measures how many times you can squeeze and relax the muscle in a short time. You tap the button with every squeeze.

sections.title: Results
sections.text: The results appear in the charts on the Progress tab. This isn't a medical measurement; it's only for tracking your own progress.

title: What does discreet mode mean?
summary: Only the circle and colours appear on the workout screen instead of text.
shortSummary: Only the circle and colours instead of text

sections.title: Discreet player
sections.text: With discreet mode on, words like SQUEEZE or RELAX don't appear on the workout screen; only the circle and colours change. You can turn it on in Profile > Training.

sections.title: Discreet notifications
sections.text: Reminder notifications come with neutral text by default; the lock screen doesn't reveal what the workout is. You can change this in Profile > Reminders.

title: Where is my data stored?
summary: All your data stays on this phone only.
shortSummary: All your data stays on this phone only

sections.title: No server
sections.text: The app has no server and no account system. Your workouts, tests and notes are stored only on this device.

sections.title: Works offline
sections.text: The whole app works without the internet. The internet is only used for purchases made through the store.

sections.title: Backup
sections.text: In Profile > My data you can export your data as a file, import it again later or delete it completely.
